To find the heat produced by a resistor, we use the formula:  
$$ Q = I^2 R t $$

Given:  
- Resistance $ R = 25 \, \Omega $  
- Current $ I = 12 \, A $  
- Time $ t = 10 \, \text{minutes} = 600 \, \text{seconds} $

$$ Q = (12)^2 \times 25 \times 600 $$  
$$ Q = 144 \times 25 \times 600 $$  
$$ Q = 3600 \times 600 $$  
$$ Q = 2,160,000 \, \text{J} = 2160 \, \text{kJ} $$

ANSWER: 2160 kJ
